title: What changes after fitting?
hook: Training accuracy is near-perfect. Does that mean validation is already high?

doesNotKnow: Delayed held-out improvement can follow near-perfect training; tiny dependent transient success is insufficient.

misconception: Must validation already be high when training is near-perfect?
objective: Compare delayed reported validation improvement with a transient dependent tiny countercase.

claims.text: The title asks what changes after fitting. The prediction asks whether validation must already be high when training is near-perfect; accuracy points/gaps are not shown before commitment. Reported observations and a saved trained countercase have distinct evidence origins. The tiny trained example briefly reached 5/5, then regressed: one new unordered pair, selected post-hoc. Published samples show delayed improvement; this countercase establishes neither stable generalization nor replication.
